bug_semantics: Authenticated cross-tenant IDOR/BOLA in the web ticket CRUD: GET /ticket/update/{id} loaded Ticket::find($id) and exposed another tenant's ticket content and attachments; POST /ticket/save accepted an attacker-selected ticket id, loaded that record without company_id scoping, then overwrote company_id with the attacker's company and saved it; GET /ticket/delete/{id} loaded and deleted any numeric ticket id without tenant scoping, and its generic Request parameter bypassed the authorization implemented by TicketDeleteRequest.
flaw_origin: The original ticket CRUD commit 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd directly introduced the first vulnerable read and save endpoints and their unscoped Ticket::find lookups. Commit 946a0c5e43a1178534e5b013ea2608d565686220 later expanded the same flaw class by adding the unscoped GET delete endpoint. Commit 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d only moved the already-vulnerable save lookup into TicketRepository and is not a BIC. Commit c837c80a4f7de40348e142af7d15e60c39ebcaf1 later created TicketDeleteRequest but did not wire it into TicketDeleteController, so it was incomplete hardening rather than the origin.
evidence: Advisory GHSA-2wg2-5v89-cgh7/CVE-2026-19539 identifies authenticated cross-company read, reassignment, and deletion before 5.4.9 and directly references commit b2b6ffdace0972ab62d1f7e8cdab0ed213bfc4a9.

Run `git show --format=fuller 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd -- app/Http/Controllers/Ticket routes/web.php`: the one-parent `Tickets CRUD` commit creates GET /ticket/update/{id} with `$ticket = Ticket::find($id)` and POST /ticket/save with `$ticket = Ticket::find($request->id)`, followed by `$ticket->company_id = Auth::user()->company_id`. Its MainController snapshot applies auth middleware, establishing the authenticated attack surface.

Run `git log 361566c1ddb01df16f2cff0aa836f04be174f3c4 -L 21,21:app/Http/Controllers/Ticket/TicketUpdateController.php` and `git log 944a9a22bb4bb82f52f3257a0b27f6d16f29d73a -L 17,17:app/Http/Controllers/Ticket/TicketSaveController.php`: each line history terminates at creation in 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd. `git log --all -S'Ticket::find($id)'` and `-S'Ticket::find($request->id)'` independently identify the same introductions; blame at the pre-fix/pre-refactor snapshots agrees.

Direct parent check: `git ls-tree -r --name-only 063d713c71ca6c453d43e7b17a9ee2f8b2fc0ce1 -- app/Http/Controllers/Ticket app/Repositories/TicketRepository.php app/Http/Requests/TicketDeleteRequest.php` returns no paths, and `git grep -n -i ticket 063d713c71ca6c453d43e7b17a9ee2f8b2fc0ce1 -- routes/web.php` returns no match. Thus the immediate parent lacks both vulnerable handlers and reachable ticket routes.

Run `git show 946a0c5e43a1178534e5b013ea2608d565686220 -- app/Http/Controllers/Ticket/TicketDeleteController.php routes/web.php`: it creates generic `delete(Request $request, int $id)`, performs unscoped `Ticket::find($id)->delete()`, and exposes GET /ticket/delete/{id}. `git log 361566c1ddb01df16f2cff0aa836f04be174f3c4 -L 15,15:app/Http/Controllers/Ticket/TicketDeleteController.php` traces that lookup to 946a0c5e43a1178534e5b013ea2608d565686220.

Run `git show 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d -- app/Http/Controllers/Ticket/TicketSaveController.php app/Repositories/TicketRepository.php`: it removes the unscoped lookup from the controller and reproduces it in a new repository, proving a refactor rather than introduction. Run `git show c837c80a4f7de40348e142af7d15e60c39ebcaf1 -- app/Http/Controllers/Ticket/TicketDeleteController.php app/Http/Requests/TicketDeleteRequest.php`: it creates a permission-checking request but makes no controller type-hint change, leaving the generic Request path active.

Run `git show --format=fuller b2b6ffdace0972ab62d1f7e8cdab0ed213bfc4a9`: the direct patch replaces all three unscoped finds with id+authenticated-company queries and firstOrFail, changes delete to TicketDeleteRequest, and adds ticket permissions and cross-tenant security tests. `git rev-parse b2b6ffdace0972ab62d1f7e8cdab0ed213bfc4a9^` is 361566c1ddb01df16f2cff0aa836f04be174f3c4, whose version.php is 5.4.8 and whose three handlers remain vulnerable.

Version boundary: b2b6ffdace0972ab62d1f7e8cdab0ed213bfc4a9 is immediately followed by 7e86b0845b14887b101a4516020fedafbff23564, whose version.php diff changes 5.4.8 to 5.4.9. `git tag --contains b2b6ffdace0972ab62d1f7e8cdab0ed213bfc4a9 --sort=version:refname` starts at v5.5.3, and v5.5.3 resolves to 584f315878b8366244c95fe3cb016b3a63f05db8 with APP_VERSION 5.5.3. `git tag --contains 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd` starts at v1.0.0, so every tagged release from v1.0.0 through the pre-fix line contains the original flaw; source version 5.4.9 and tagged v5.5.3 contain the fix.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file commit 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd` shows author and committer Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com>, one parent 063d713c71ca6c453d43e7b17a9ee2f8b2fc0ce1, and message exactly `Tickets CRUD`, with no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker. Later Claude-marked hardening/fix commits are not evidence about the BIC.
reasoning: The smallest commit that first made this advisory's core vulnerability real is the original 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd CRUD implementation: it simultaneously made attacker-controlled ticket ids reachable for cross-tenant read and ownership-changing save, while its immediate parent had no ticket handlers or routes. The later delete commit broadened impact, the repository extraction preserved an existing flaw, and the 2026 request creation merely failed to close it. The advisory-linked b2b6ffdace0972ab62d1f7e8cdab0ed213bfc4a9 is the direct complete fix and defines the 5.4.8/5.4.9 source boundary. Because the BIC commit object contains no AI signal and identifies a human author/committer, the protocol requires NOT_AI; AI trailers on later incomplete hardening, version bumps, or the fix are excluded.
